home.name: Yerevan
home.note: City centre (OSM Nominatim administrative). Mos sample 40.1792, 44.4991 is within ~1 km; this file uses the cited Nominatim point.

places.name: Garni Temple
places.description: A reconstructed Ionic temple stands on a basalt cliff above the Azat gorge in Garni. Walk the platform for columns against the canyon and the surrounding fortress walls.

places.name: Geghard Monastery
places.description: Geghard’s churches and rock-cut chambers sit in a mountain gorge east of Yerevan. Some chapels are carved straight into the cliff, with light falling through openings in the stone.

places.name: Etchmiadzin Cathedral
places.description: The Mother See cathedral in Vagharshapat is the spiritual centre of the Armenian Apostolic Church. The complex of churches and museums surrounds a courtyard open to visitors.
places.photo_credit: Author of the photo is Heretiq · Public domain
places.image_credit: Author of the photo is Heretiq · Public domain

places.name: Amberd Fortress
places.description: Amberd’s stone walls crown a ridge on the slopes of Mount Aragats. A medieval church stands inside the fortress ruins with wide views over the highland valleys.

places.name: Zvartnots Cathedral
places.description: The ruined circular cathedral of Zvartnots sits in an open archaeological park west of Yerevan. Walk among the column bases and carved stones with Ararat on the horizon on clear days.

places.name: Mount Ararat
places.description: From Khor Virap monastery on Armenia’s Ararat plain, Mount Ararat fills the southern sky. The stamp uses this Armenian viewpoint; the summit itself lies across the border in Türkiye.

places.name: Cascade
places.description: Yerevan’s Cascade climbs in limestone terraces from Tamanyan sculpture park toward the Monument district. Escalators inside help you rise between outdoor art platforms and city views.

places.name: Republic Square
places.description: Republic Square is Yerevan’s main oval plaza of pink tufa government buildings and museums. In the evening the fountains and facades light up for a slow walk around the oval.

places.name: Vernissage
places.description: Vernissage is Yerevan’s open-air market for crafts, art, and souvenirs along Khanjyan and nearby streets. Weekend stalls are the busiest for handmade pieces and Soviet-era finds.

places.name: GUM Market
places.description: GUM Market on Khorenatsi is a covered hall of spice, produce, and prepared-food counters. Wander the aisles for dried fruit, cheese, and a quick taste of Yerevan’s market culture.

places.name: Dolmama
places.description: Dolmama is a long-running restaurant on Pushkin Street known for refined takes on Armenian home cooking. The stamp marks the venue location — check current hours before you go.

places.name: Pandok Yerevan
places.description: Pandok Yerevan (Tavern Yerevan) on Zakyan Street serves hearty Armenian tavern fare in the city centre. Come for grilled meats and shared plates in a casual setting.

places.name: Sherep
places.description: Sherep sits near Republic Square and focuses on contemporary Armenian cooking. The stamp uses the mapped restaurant point on Pap Tagavor Street.
places.photo_credit: Shaun Dunphy from Lindfield, United Kingdom · CC BY-SA 2.0
places.image_credit: Shaun Dunphy from Lindfield, United Kingdom · CC BY-SA 2.0

places.name: Lavash
places.description: Lavash restaurant on Tumanyan Street is named for Armenia’s flatbread and serves modern Armenian dishes. Confirm opening times on the day you visit.
places.photo_credit: Shaun Dunphy from Lindfield, United Kingdom · CC BY-SA 2.0
places.image_credit: Shaun Dunphy from Lindfield, United Kingdom · CC BY-SA 2.0

places.name: In Vino
places.description: In Vino on Saryan Street is a well-known wine bar in Yerevan’s wine-bar strip. Taste Armenian bottles by the glass in a compact, walk-in space.

places.name: The Club
places.description: The Club (Akumb) on Tumanyan Street mixes dining with a cultural-club atmosphere in central Yerevan. Use the mapped point; programmes and hours can change.

places.name: Pak Shuka
places.description: Pak Shuka (the Covered Market) on Mashtots Avenue is a classic Yerevan food market for produce and pantry goods. Browse the counters for fruit, herbs, and picnic supplies.

places.name: Caucasus Pandok
places.description: Caucasus Pandok on Hanrapetutyan Street serves Caucasian and Armenian tavern dishes in central Yerevan. A straightforward stop for shared plates and grilled food.

places.name: Dargett Craft Beer
places.description: Dargett is a Yerevan craft brewery taproom on Aram Street. Stop in for house beers on tap; the stamp marks the brewpub node, not a beer brand partnership.

places.name: Yerevan Wine Days
places.description: Yerevan Wine Days turns Saryan, Tumanyan, and Moskovyan streets into an open-air wine festival, usually on the first weekend of June. It is seasonal and limited to those festival days — check yerewinedays.am for the current dates.

places.name: Sevanavank
places.description: A monastic peninsula on Lake Sevan with twin churches above the water.

places.name: Colosseum
places.description: Rome’s great amphitheatre still stands in the heart of the ancient city. Walk the outer rings and arches to feel how crowds once poured in for public games.

places.name: Trevi Fountain
places.description: The Trevi Fountain fills a tight square in central Rome with cascading water and baroque sculpture. Tradition says toss a coin over your shoulder if you hope to return.

places.name: Pantheon
places.description: A Roman temple later consecrated as a church, the Pantheon is famous for its concrete dome and open oculus. Inside, a calm circular hall is lit by a single shaft of daylight from above.

places.name: Milan Cathedral
places.description: Milan’s Gothic cathedral fills Piazza del Duomo with marble spires and a wide facade. Climb toward the terraces for close views of the statues and the city beyond.

places.name: Florence Cathedral
places.description: Santa Maria del Fiore anchors Florence’s historic centre with Brunelleschi’s great dome. The patterned marble facade and baptistery sit around Piazza del Duomo.

places.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
places.description: The freestanding bell tower of Pisa’s cathedral leans across the green Campo dei Miracoli. Walk the lawn for the classic view of tower, duomo, and baptistery together.

places.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
places.description: Hadrian’s mausoleum later became a fortress and papal refuge on the Tiber. From the ramparts you look along the bridge of angels toward St Peter’s.

places.name: Pompeii
places.description: The buried Roman city of Pompeii opens as a vast archaeological park at the foot of Vesuvius. Streets, houses, and the forum still show daily life frozen by the eruption.

places.name: Pizza al taglio
places.description: Stampd treats pizza as a Naples city food stamp — not a named restaurant. This photo shows classic Margherita-style pizza as a stand-in for the street-food culture the stamp celebrates.

places.name: Gelato
places.description: Stampd treats gelato as a Rome city food stamp — not a specific gelateria. The photo is a representative Italian artisanal gelato display for that food-culture stamp.

places.name: Mercato Centrale
places.description: Florence’s central market hall gathers produce stalls downstairs and a busy food court above. Come for Tuscan ingredients, sandwiches, and a sit-down bite under the iron roof.

places.name: Spanish Steps
places.description: A broad Baroque stair climbs from Piazza di Spagna toward the Trinità dei Monti church. Sit on a lower step to watch the square, then walk up for the view over the rooftops.
places.photo_credit: Please credit "Family photos of Infrogmation" · CC BY 2.5
places.image_credit: Please credit "Family photos of Infrogmation" · CC BY 2.5

places.name: Villa Borghese
places.description: Villa Borghese is Rome’s great central park of lawns, tree avenues, and museum villas. Rent a bike or stroll to the lake temple for a quieter hour away from the densest streets.

places.name: Ponte Vecchio
places.description: Florence’s medieval bridge still carries shops across the Arno in a tight row of windows. Cross at dusk when the river reflects the goldsmith shutters and the corridor above.

places.name: Piazza Navona
places.description: An elongated square follows the shape of Domitian’s stadium, lined with cafés and fountains. Bernini’s Fountain of the Four Rivers anchors the middle of the open space.

places.name: Rialto Bridge
places.description: The stone arch of the Rialto is the oldest of the Grand Canal’s four bridges. Climb the steps for the classic view of water traffic and the market side of San Polo.

places.name: Positano
places.description: Positano spills down the Amalfi cliffs in stacked pastel houses above a small beach. Walk the steep lanes for sea views and the harbour square at the bottom.

places.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
places.description: Milan’s 19th-century glass-roofed arcade links Piazza del Duomo to Piazza della Scala. Look up at the iron-and-glass vault and the mosaic floor under the central octagon.

places.name: Venice Carnival
places.description: Venice Carnival fills the city with costumes and masks before Lent, with many public moments in and around Piazza San Marco. It is seasonal and date-limited each year — check the official calendar before you go.

places.name: Palio di Siena
places.description: Twice each summer, Siena’s contrade race bareback around Piazza del Campo in the Palio. The square is packed for trial runs and the race days in July and August — a short, seasonal tradition, not a year-round show.

places.name: Mercato di Testaccio
places.description: A neighbourhood market hall in Testaccio with produce stalls and casual lunch counters.

places.name: Porta Palazzo Market
places.description: One of Europe’s large open-air markets spreads around Piazza della Repubblica in Turin.

places.name: Sensō-ji
places.description: Tokyo’s oldest temple approach runs through Nakamise-dōri to a red hōzōmon gate.

places.name: Fushimi Inari Shrine
places.description: Thousands of vermilion torii gates climb the trails of Mount Inari.

places.name: Osaka Castle

places.name: Himeji Castle
places.description: A white original castle complex often called Japan’s finest surviving keep.

places.name: Tōdai-ji
places.description: A vast wooden hall houses a giant Buddha statue in Nara Park.

places.name: Arashiyama bamboo grove
places.description: A walking path through towering bamboo west of central Kyoto.

places.name: Mount Fuji from Kawaguchiko
places.description: Lakeside viewpoints frame Japan’s iconic peak north of the mountain.

places.name: Shibuya Crossing
places.description: A famous scramble intersection outside Shibuya Station.

places.name: Itsukushima Shrine
places.description: A floating-looking torii stands in the tidal flats of Miyajima.

places.name: Shirakawa-go
places.description: Thatched gasshō-zukuri farmhouses fill a mountain village.

places.name: Kuromon Market
places.description: A covered market for seafood, produce and ready-to-eat skewers.

places.name: Nishiki Market
places.description: Kyoto’s narrow ‘kitchen’ street sells pickles, tofu and snacks.

places.name: Toyosu / Tsukiji outer stalls
places.description: Sushi counters and kitchenware shops continue around the former Tsukiji site and new Toyosu market.

places.description: The Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité is undergoing restoration after the 2019 fire; façades remain a landmark.

places.description: Louis XIV’s château opens onto formal gardens and the Hall of Mirrors. Arrive early for shorter queues.

places.name: Stonehenge
